The global **COVID-19 pandemic** (also known as the **coronavirus pandemic**), caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), began with an outbreak in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) on 30 January 2020 and assessed it as having become a pandemic on 11 March. The WHO declared that the public health emergency caused by COVID-19 had ended in May 2023, while noting that COVID-19 continued to be a global health threat.

Covid-19: Fresh Surge in Asia —What’s Behind the Rise? | Covid Cases | Covid 19 2025 | Covid 19 News
The Financial Express
410000 subscribers
56 likes
7348 views
21 May 2025
Covid-19 cases are once again climbing across parts of Asia, with countries such as Singapore, Hong Kong, China, and Thailand seeing a sharp uptick, largely driven by new subvariants of the JN.1 strain. In Singapore, weekly cases rose from 11,100 to 14,200, alongside a noticeable increase in hospitalisations. Health officials attribute the surge to waning immunity and the emergence of immune-evasive variants like LF.7 and NB.1.8. Although there is currently no indication of more severe illness, experts caution that the wave could soon extend to India, where active cases remain relatively low but are beginning to show a mild upward trend.
